title: American Law Enforcement Heroes Act of 2017
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the Senate reported version is repeated here.)

American Law Enforcement Heroes Act of 2017

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to include as an allowable use of grant funds under the Community Oriented Policing Services program prioritizing the hiring and training of veterans as career law enforcement officers.

summary.headline: A 2017 law lets federal Community Oriented Policing Services grant money be used to prioritize hiring and training veterans as career police officers.
summary.what_it_does: The law amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968. It adds a new permitted use for COPS program grant funds: prioritizing the hiring and training of veterans as career law enforcement officers. The summary does not describe how grant recipients must apply this priority.

who_it_affects.group: Military veterans seeking careers in law enforcement
who_it_affects.how: Local agencies that receive COPS grants may use the funds to give veterans priority in hiring and training for law enforcement jobs.

who_it_affects.group: State and local police and sheriff's departments that apply for COPS grants
who_it_affects.how: They may use COPS grant money to fund hiring and training programs that prioritize veterans.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted June 2, 2017. The summary does not state a separate effective date.
